summary: Recover exact owned invalid usage indexes after concurrent interruption

delivery.outcome: Complete issue142 after the observed SQLSTATE55P03: independently publish explicit OID/definition/digest-bound concurrent recovery for a component-owned invalid usage index, then repair the exact known failed index52788 and resume bounded additive archive indexing with native query readback.
nonGoals: No DROP command, data deletion, arbitrary SQL, unknown/constraint/healthy-index repair, automatic repair from ordinary apply, provider-policy, credential, dependency or release change. No query deadline increase.

architecture.decision: Keep normal plan/apply fail closed on invalid indexes. Explicit recovery observes one managed nonunique invalid leaf index, binds its exact database/OID/logical definition, and executes REINDEX INDEX CONCURRENTLY with bounded time/resources and no automatic cleanup/retry. Preserve logical schema and rows. Raise only the separately bounded DDL lock wait to5000ms after the measured250ms interruption; query deadline remains5000ms.
interfaceChanges: Explicit recover-plan/recover operations within the native usage-index module CLI

dataChanges.description: Concurrent physical rebuild of the exact known component-owned invalid nonunique index, preserving logical definition and all archive data; remaining additive leaf indexing remains explicit.

architecture.rollback: Protected source revert; known invalid/partial objects are preserved and reported, with no automatic drop or unknown-object change.

commands: python -m ruff check --no-respect-gitignore src tests integration
validation.evidence: Unit tests without optional driver, genuine interrupted concurrent-build fixture and bounded recovery, old-OID/conflicting/constraint/healthy guards, full stack/protected exact-head source merge, then exact local recovery and all-partition query/index readback.
